# The MacEx Journal

> Practical Mac file organization and productivity articles by MacEx.
- [System Data vs Purgeable Space on Mac](https://macex.app/blog/system-data-vs-purgeable-space-mac/): System Data and purgeable space are not the same. Learn why Storage and Disk Utility show different Mac space totals, and what to do safely on your Mac.

- [Where Mac screenshots are saved, and how to stop the pile-up](https://macex.app/blog/where-mac-screenshots-are-saved/): Mac screenshots land on the Desktop by default. Change the save location in two clicks, then clean up the ones you already have without losing anything.
- [Spotlight not finding files on Mac: what to check first](https://macex.app/blog/spotlight-not-finding-files-mac/): A file you know exists is missing from Spotlight. Check the folder, Search Privacy and result settings, then rebuild the index, in that order.
- [How to Find Large Files on Your Mac](https://macex.app/blog/find-large-files-on-mac/): Running out of Mac storage? Find your biggest files with Storage settings and Finder, then remove what you no longer need without deleting the wrong thing.
- [Can you delete DMG files on a Mac? When it is safe](https://macex.app/blog/can-you-delete-dmg-files-on-mac/): A DMG is only the container an app came in. Once the app is in Applications you can usually delete it. Here is how to check, and when to keep one.
- [A Mac file naming system you can actually keep using](https://macex.app/blog/mac-file-naming-system/): Make project files easier to recognize with a simple subject, date and version pattern, with examples for invoices, drafts, screenshots and shared work.
- [Finder Smart Folders: a project view without moving files](https://macex.app/blog/finder-smart-folders/): Build a saved Finder search for active work, understand what Smart Folders actually store, and choose rules that stay useful as your projects grow.
- [How to find a file on your Mac when you forgot its name](https://macex.app/blog/find-files-on-mac-without-filename/): Turn the clues you remember into a useful search: file type, approximate date, likely location, and content. A practical workflow for Finder and MacEx.
